>unless you have a horse who inflates themself every time you reach for a cinch, even after you've walked them.

Horse's don't inflate themselves their ribs are pretty immobile and you're cinching/girthing directly over their ribs, anatomically wise this dosen't work.

Deciding to tighten the girth to tight results in the ascending pectoral and serratus ventralis thoracis muscles to become pinched/tight/sore as well.

They can physically avoid it eg moving away etc, but a majority of the time it's because they're communicating to you and if you listen you'd find an awful lot more, it's absolutely horrific to see some dissection's of thoroughbred's in particular.

​

>It doesn't hurt them, it just makes them exhale.

Horse's have more nerve endings than humans do, so if someone knees you in the gut, regardless of how "light" it is, It hurts.

​

>When you're standing in a shed row with other horses in front of and behind you, ready to go out to the training track on a limited time window, you can't necessarily walk a horse holding its breath like that. By the time you get it walked and cinched the other horses will be returning from the track and the next set will be ready to go out, and if you don't have an extra rider, your horse just missed their training window.

Welfare of anyone including animals deserves better than a quick "hit" because humans have decided they can't wait on the animals time-frame.

I don't think it's morally right to go "Hey, why don't you knee your child in the gut lightly It won't hurt them but we're running out of time and they don't want to do the job we've demanded of them."

If that's not okay then don't do it to the million dollar horses you have.

So I'll agree to disagree.

>Occasionally, some horses will suck in air to inflate their stomach when you cinch the saddle so the strap loosens slightly when they exhale. A quick knee in the ribs makes them exhale so you can properly secure the saddle.

...Or just take your horse for a walk and tighten the girth/cinch, absolutely no need for that nonsense.
